what_its_for: Docusate is a stool softener used to prevent or treat constipation. It works by pulling water into your stool to make it softer and easier to pass. It is often used when you should avoid straining during a bowel movement, such as after surgery, childbirth, or a heart attack.
how_to_take: Take docusate by mouth with a full glass of water (8 ounces). You may take it with or without food. Swallow capsules whole — do not crush or chew them. If you are taking the liquid form, measure your dose carefully using a medicine spoon or dosing cup. Drink plenty of fluids throughout the day (6 to 8 glasses of water) to help it work better.
dosing: Adults and children 12 years and older: The usual dose is 50 to 300 mg per day, taken as a single dose or divided into smaller doses. Children 2 to 11 years: 50 to 150 mg per day, divided into doses. Children under 2 years: Only use under a doctor's direction. Always follow your doctor's or pharmacist's specific instructions, as your dose may be different.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep away from heat, light, and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children. Do not use if the expiration date on the package has passed.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking mineral oil at the same time as docusate, as this combination may cause unwanted side effects. Do not use other laxatives unless your doctor tells you to. Avoid foods that can worsen constipation, such as processed foods low in fiber. Do not use docusate for more than 1 week unless directed by your doctor.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor if you experience: stomach pain, cramping, or nausea; rectal bleeding; no bowel movement after 1 week of using this medicine; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing; or if your constipation keeps coming back. Seek emergency care right away if you have severe abdominal pain or you cannot pass gas or stool.
when_it_works: Docusate usually starts to work within 12 to 72 hours (1 to 3 days) after taking it. It is not a fast-acting laxative, so be patient. If you do not see results within 1 week, contact your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Docusate is generally considered safe to use during pregnancy, but always check with your doctor before taking any medicine while pregnant. Breastfeeding: Docusate passes into breast milk in very small amounts and is generally considered safe, but talk to your doctor first. Older adults: Older adults may be more likely to become dehydrated. Be sure to drink plenty of fluids. Children under 2 years: Do not use without a doctor's guidance. Kidney or liver disease: Talk to your doctor before using if you have kidney or liver problems.
